newsitem.title: GERMANY: Porsche says 1995/96 profits higher than expected.
newsitem.headline: Porsche says 1995/96 profits higher than expected.

text.p: German sportscar maker Porsche AG said on Thursday that it expected to report a profit of about 40 to 50 million marks for its 1995/96 business year that ends July 31.

Porsche said its profits during the first six months of its business year totalled 10.3 million marks and said the gains in the second half were due to cost-saving measures along with worldwide strong demand for versions of its 911 model.
Sales during the business year rose to about 2.8 billion marks compared with 2.61 billion marks in 1994/95. Porsche said final results for the year will be released on November 6.

Porsche said its supervisory board would decide at a meeting on November 6 on whether to resume paying a dividend. Porsche last paid a dividend in its 1991/92 business year of 2.50 marks for each 50-mark nominal share.
Porsche also said the contract of management board chairman Wendelin Wiedeking has been extended for another five years effective from October 1, 1997.
The carmaker said it produced 20,132 vehicles of the 911 model, up from 17,293 vehicles in the previous financial year, in reaching a new production record for the car since 1963.
Worldwide sales of the 911 during 1995/96 business year totalled 19,096 vehicles, up from 17,407 vehicles in the prior business year and more than triple the level in 1992/93.
